source.title: Muon Sublates the Edge of Stability in LLM Pretraining
source.authors: Yan-Zhe Chen; Qifang Zhao; Xiao-Xiao Xu; Fang-Hui Liu

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including main text and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Measures Muon loss balance and consecutive update alignment in controlled networks and language-model pretraining, relevant to V5's stability and alignment signatures but using Muon-specific diagnostics and recipes.
record.gate_note: The study's results test only V5's loss/alignment behavior under Muon. CIFAR training-loss-to-zero, spurious-minimum width, shortcuts/depth, initialization, and batch-normalization speed claims are not tested. Cited prior work is not recorded as study results. The 1B run measures loss and alignment but lacks conditional T1 probes.
record.test_reason: The study measures Muon-specific conditional loss balance and update-direction alignment. Its finite-step directional curvature is not V5's sharpness or initial linearized-model stability limit. It does not test recovery above that limit, eventual divergence, or full-batch GD sharpness tracking. Temporal reversal is also not a prediction named in V5. These results address a related optimization claim, rather than any version supplied.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that no-momentum Muon separates conditional loss balance from temporal alignment. Controlled experiments and 130M probes show loss-boundary tracking; 130M alignment is weakly negative, while the studied 1B configuration shows stronger partial cancellation, with training continuing to improve. The 1B run has no conditional loss-boundary probes, and the conclusions do not establish the same behavior for momentum Muon.
record.recipe_differences: Uses stochastic no-momentum exact-polar Muon in controlled MLP/CNN/Transformer runs and practical no-momentum NS-5 Muon with AdamW on auxiliary parameters in LLM pretraining. It measures loss-boundary tracking and direction cosines rather than the original GD stability-threshold recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes coherence and temporal alignment; learning-rate perturbations change conditional loss response while alignment remains negative; temporal alignment varies across layers and between 130M and 1B configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Controlled exact-polar Muon runs approach a coherence-corrected conditional loss-neutral boundary. Practical 130M Muon-only probes repeatedly lie near the analogous finite-reference boundary.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: No-momentum Muon can exhibit conditional loss-boundary tracking under its own directional-curvature diagnostic.

fits_no_version.finding: At the shared 22M checkpoint, reducing the Muon rate produces a negative conditional loss increment and increasing it produces a positive increment, while sampled temporal alignment remains negative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Muon conditional loss balance and negative consecutive-direction alignment are distinct signals.

fits_no_version.finding: 130M directions have weak negative alignment; the studied 1B configuration has stronger cancellation while remaining far from reversal. Frozen-state and temporal comparisons reveal a negative trajectory bias beyond independent-batch dispersion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: No-momentum Muon's temporal alignment depends on sampling and evolving training state, with magnitude varying across configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: All-AdamW and momentum-Muon controls have positive mean displacement cosines of 0.893 and 0.713.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The negative temporal alignment observed with no-momentum Muon does not extend to these optimizer controls.

record.problems: The 1B run has no conditional T1 probes. LLM experiments use approximate NS-5 and one-seed observations; intervals are pointwise probe uncertainty and do not measure across-seed variability. Cross-scale comparisons do not isolate batch size. Controlled-network first-event detection uses no persistence filtering. Some trajectory values are only shown in figures.
record.rows_left_out: None. The study reports other figure-only trajectories and layer-specific alignment plots, but these were not added as separate rows because the main-text aggregate statements and conditions are captured, and figure-only per-layer values are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR-10/100 training classification error under SGD or Adam, including random or corrupted labels and size, regularization, and duration conditions.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through extra student width.
Depth-related training degradation, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Comparative effects of initialization on signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Recovery above the initial linearized-model stability limit, curvature reduction during the catapult phase, divergence at larger rates, full-batch GD sharpness tracking, and divergence from below the threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V5 verdicts. A different optimizer alone need not disqualify a test, but these diagnostics do not measure the effects V5 specifies. The supplied versions also contain no prediction of coherent update reversal. States marked cannot_determine refer to the supplied claim versions, not to whether the paper observed its own diagnostic effects.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 training classification error; random or corrupted labels; model size, optimizer, and training-duration conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization and student-width effects on spurious minima.
Plain versus residual network training error; shortcuts, normalization, and depth effects.
Initialization-dependent signal propagation, training speed, and maximum trainable depth.

The study does not test the claimed squared-loss wide-network GD catapult mechanism, the full-batch GD sharpness threshold, or divergence from below the threshold. It tests Muon loss neutrality and temporal alignment, not a general stability threshold.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual training without normalization.

rows.subject: MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured conditional effective curvature against the coherence-corrected loss-neutral boundary across batch sizes.
rows.measure: Conditional curvature ŝM_b versus boundary 2ρ̂_b/η; authors report curvature approaches and oscillates around the boundary.
rows.value: Near-boundary tracking; no numeric summary stated.
rows.uncertainty: 95% Monte Carlo intervals described in Appendix B.5; no row-specific interval stated.
rows.note: Controlled-network validation uses SVD-polar updates; the main text names plotted batches 64, 512, and full.
rows.check: Tracks Muon's normalized finite-step directional curvature against its conditional loss-neutral boundary, not V5's stability threshold or sharpness. The reported tracking is observed for this separate measure.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured conditional effective curvature against the coherence-corrected loss-neutral boundary across batch sizes.
rows.measure: Conditional curvature ŝM_b versus boundary 2ρ̂_b/η; authors report curvature approaches and oscillates around the boundary.
rows.value: Near-boundary tracking; no numeric summary stated.
rows.uncertainty: 95% Monte Carlo intervals described in Appendix B.5; no row-specific interval stated.
rows.check: Muon loss-boundary tracking does not establish V5's sharpness behavior or recovery above an initial stability limit. CIFAR squared training loss also does not establish V1's training classification error.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured conditional effective curvature against the coherence-corrected loss-neutral boundary across batch sizes.
rows.measure: Conditional curvature ŝM_b versus boundary 2ρ̂_b/η; authors report curvature approaches and oscillates around the boundary.
rows.value: Near-boundary tracking; no numeric summary stated.
rows.uncertainty: 95% Monte Carlo intervals described in Appendix B.5; no row-specific interval stated.
rows.check: Measures Muon loss balance rather than V5's stability behavior. Appendix B.6 specifies batches 16, 512, and full for the main Transformer T1 panel; batch 128 belongs to the directional-alignment panels and appendix grid.

rows.subject: 130M Llama-like LLM
rows.operation_detail: Tracked conditional curvature and coherence-corrected boundary during no-momentum NS-5 Muon pretraining.
rows.measure: Conditional curvature ŝM_k,32 versus 2ρ̂_k,32/η_k; boundary tracking implies conditional mean reference-loss increment near zero.
rows.value: Curvature repeatedly lies near the boundary, including during constant-learning-rate stage.
rows.uncertainty: Eight probe draws; pointwise 95% intervals described, without a row-specific estimate.
rows.note: This is conditional Muon-only probing; complete Muon-plus-AdamW runs improve validation loss over longer horizons.
rows.check: Conditional Muon-only finite-reference loss balance does not measure a stability threshold for the complete stochastic Muon-plus-AdamW training run. Figure 1e is the 0.02 run; Figure 5a is the separate 0.04 run.

rows.subject: 130M Llama-like LLM
rows.operation_detail: Measured global cosine between consecutive no-momentum NS-5 Muon directions.
rows.measure: Median consecutive-direction cosine; directions are negatively aligned but far from exact reversal.
rows.baseline: Exact reversal at −1 is the stated reference.
rows.value: Full-horizon cosine medians range from −0.048 to −0.032.
rows.note: Aggregate stated across all four runs; no individual run medians are assigned.
rows.check: Consecutive-direction cosine measures temporal alignment. V5 does not predict exact reversal, so distance from −1 cannot be scored as partial evidence for V5.

rows.subject: 130M Llama-like LLM
rows.operation_detail: Measured conditional curvature and coherence-corrected boundary at fixed checkpoints for differing peak learning rates.
rows.measure: Reference-gradient coherence ρ̂_k,b and corresponding 2ρ̂_k,b/η_k trajectories.
rows.value: Larger probe batches generally strengthen reference-gradient coherence and shift the boundary trajectories.
rows.note: Probe batch size varies at fixed checkpoints; it does not vary training batch size.
rows.check: Probe-batch coherence is a separate diagnostic and does not establish V5's stability behavior. Figure 6 includes peak learning rate 0.02 as well as 0.04, 0.08, and 0.12. Probe batch size changes at fixed checkpoints; training batch size remains 32.

rows.subject: 22M Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared conditional loss increment under Muon learning-rate branches from a shared checkpoint.
rows.uncertainty: 95% intervals as stated for each branch.
rows.locator: Appendix C.1, Table 2; Section 3.2; Appendix C.3
rows.note: Authors state halving the rate moves the conditional step to the loss-decrease side of T1 and doubling it to the loss-increase side.
rows.check: The numbers correctly describe one-step Muon-only loss responses at a shared state. A positive conditional increment at rate 0.08 does not establish exceeding an initial linearized stability limit, a catapult trajectory, recovery to low loss, or divergence.

rows.subject: 22M Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured consecutive Muon-direction cosines during learning-rate branches.
rows.measure: Mean sampled cosine between consecutive directions; all five branches had negative observations over the stated interval.
rows.value: Means −0.064, −0.100, and −0.117 at rates 0.02, 0.04, and 0.08; 480 negative observations over 4,000 ≤ k < 6,400 across five branches.
rows.note: Authors caution these signs describe sampled pairs, not every step.
rows.check: Negative temporal cosine does not measure any supplied version. Clarify that each of the five branches has 480 negative sampled observations over 4000 ≤ k < 6400; this is not 480 observations pooled across branches.

rows.subject: 130M Llama-like LLM
rows.operation_detail: Measured global consecutive-direction cosine after checkpoint learning-rate changes.
rows.measure: Global cosine response; increasing rate initially makes alignment more negative and decreasing rate makes it less negative, then both tend back toward pre-perturbation value.
rows.baseline: Pre-perturbation cosine trajectory; numeric value not stated.
rows.value: Figure-only trajectory and textual directional description; no numeric cosine values stated.
rows.note: 130M perturbation branches have no conditional T1 probes; validation loss improves over full continuation.
rows.check: Alignment responses to learning-rate changes do not establish V5's stability or recovery behavior. The 130M branches have no conditional loss-boundary probes.

rows.subject: 1B Llama-like model
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and validation loss during no-momentum NS-5 Muon pretraining.
rows.measure: Training and validation cross-entropy loss over training.
rows.value: Loss continues to improve despite partial cancellation between successive directions; no conditional T1 probe was performed.
rows.note: Loss trend alone does not measure whether the loss-neutral boundary is reached.
rows.check: Improving language-model cross-entropy alone establishes neither V1's near-zero CIFAR classification error nor V5's loss trajectory relative to a measured stability limit.

rows.subject: 1B Llama-like model
rows.operation_detail: Measured global cosine between consecutive Muon directions.
rows.measure: Global consecutive-direction cosine; stronger partial cancellation than 130M, remaining far from coherent reversal.
rows.baseline: Exact reversal at −1 is the stated reference; 130M cross-scale comparator is −0.048 to −0.032 median.
rows.value: Figure-only cosine trajectory; text describes more negative global alignment than 130M and far from −1.
rows.note: Text explicitly says cross-scale comparison alone does not isolate batch size because model and training configuration also change.
rows.check: Partial directional cancellation is not a partial occurrence of V5. The cross-scale comparison changes model and training configuration as well as batch size.

rows.subject: Tiny Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared fixed-state pairwise batch-direction cosine with consecutive temporal cosine.
rows.measure: Frozen-state mean cosine and temporal mean cosine between consecutive directions.
rows.baseline: Frozen-state means positive: ranges 0.0172 to 0.1153 (seed 1337) and 0.0170 to 0.1189 (seed 2026).
rows.value: Temporal means −0.0314 and −0.0324; 99.91% and 99.70% of pairs negative.
rows.uncertainty: Frozen-state pairwise probes use 95% delete-one-batch jackknife intervals; numeric bounds not stated here. No across-seed uncertainty.
rows.note: Joint Muon and AdamW trajectory updates prevent attributing feedback to either optimizer alone.
rows.check: Frozen-state versus temporal cosine measures sampling dispersion and trajectory feedback, neither of which is a supplied claim version. Joint optimizer updates prevent attributing the feedback to Muon alone.

rows.subject: 130M Llama-like model, all-AdamW baseline
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine between consecutive attention and FFN matrix-parameter displacements.
rows.note: Comparator uses AdamW displacements, not the no-momentum Muon direction diagnostic.
rows.check: The 0.893 displacement cosine is an optimizer control for temporal alignment, not a measure of V5's stability threshold.

rows.subject: 130M Llama-like model, momentum Muon
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine between consecutive attention and FFN matrix-parameter displacements.
rows.note: Comparator uses momentum Muon displacement cosine; it does not test V5's stated GD stability-threshold behavior.
rows.check: The 0.713 displacement cosine is an optimizer control for temporal alignment, not a measure of V5's stability threshold.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Controlled MLP, CNN, and Transformer exact-polar runs; 130M no-momentum NS-5 Muon pretraining
reader_labels.reason: The conditional curvature approaches the coherence-corrected loss-neutral boundary in controlled networks and repeatedly tracks it in the 130M run (R1–R4). The study's Muon-specific edge is accompanied by continued training progress.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: 22M learning-rate branches and 130M/1B temporal alignment measurements
reader_labels.reason: Loss response and temporal alignment separate: 22M branches change conditional loss-increment sign while sampled temporal cosines remain negative; 130M is weakly negative and 1B is more negative but still far from −1 (R7–R11). The stability signature differs under Muon from the GD version stated in the claim.
